message.content:
**Order filled: bought 40 shares of AAPL at $222.90 (≈$8,916).**

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (filed 2024-11-01), this morning's feed, and the latest news, then bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.90, which filled at $222.90 for about $8,916 — comfortably inside the $10,000 per-order cap, the only order today (so well under the $20,000 daily total), and funded entirely from the $50,000 cash balance with no money leaving the account. The fundamentals supported a buy: FY2024 total net sales of $391,035 million (up 2% from $383,285 million), operating income of $123,216 million, net income of $93,736 million and diluted EPS of $6.08, with operating cash flow of $118,254 million — and importantly, net income was depressed by a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the ECJ's State Aid ruling, so underlying profitability actually improved (operating income rose ~7.8% and gross margin expanded to 46.2% from 44.1%, helped by Services revenue up 13% to $96,169 million at 73.9% gross margin). The Q4 release showed revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, indicating reacceleration, and the balance sheet remains fortress-like with $140.8 billion of cash and marketable securities plus a $110 billion buyback authorization. The feed and news were neutral-to-mildly positive — shares drifting in a tight $220–222 range on light volume, headlines noting steady iPhone 16 supplier builds into December, unchanged holiday-quarter analyst estimates, and investors weighing iPhone 16 demand and the Apple Intelligence rollout — so I sized the position modestly rather than aggressively. I did note the real risks in the filing (Greater China net sales down 8% to $66,952 million, DOJ and EU DMA antitrust exposure with potential fines up to 10% of worldwide net sales, and supply-chain concentration), which is why I kept the order small and used a limit price just above the $222.70 last trade to ensure a fill without chasing.

Order filled at 222.90, 40 shares = $8,916. Within $10k per order and $20k total. Cash was $50,000, so no money moved out.
